title: Unresponsive but breathing normally
summary: Call emergency services, maintain an open airway, and monitor continuously.
sources: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care — Recovery Position
2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Positioning of the Ill or Injured Person
actions: Call emergency services immediately and keep checking for normal breathing.
If serious spine, hip, or pelvic injury is not suspected, place the person on their side in the recovery position with the airway open and mouth directed downward.
If major trauma is possible, avoid unnecessary movement, but airway and breathing take priority. Turn as a unit with help if vomiting or airway obstruction requires it.
Loosen tight clothing, keep warm, and look for a medical alert identifier or medicine container without delaying care.
If breathing becomes absent or abnormal, roll onto the back on a firm surface and start CPR and an AED.
prohibitions: Do not give food, drink, or oral medicine.
Do not leave the person alone.
Do not let concern about the spine prevent essential airway care.

emergencyCall.text: Unresponsiveness requires emergency assessment even when breathing is normal.
